messages:
Maria G: FYI support case #8571 — tenant acme-retail hitting 429s on our dedicated pool (gpu-pool-7). Started ~08:12 UTC. Symptoms: sudden token regen spikes, elevated kv_evictions/sec, and auth throttles. Logs attached. @Jamal R can you take a look?

Jamal R: on it. Can you paste the eviction log snippet and slab stats? Any long-context traffic patterns from that tenant?

Maria G: pasted log snippet: ```EVICT TRACE 08:13:02 node=g7-12 tenant=acme-retail key=ctx:session:9f3a len=158432 slab_used=188MB slab_free=12MB frag=0.43 evict_reason=memory_pressure regen_count=4``` Also saw regen bursts: 50+ regen ops in a 60s window.

Ingrid S: I pulled metrics — node g7-12 had kv_evictions/sec spike to ~210 at 08:14. Heap at ~92%. Notable: 3 concurrent long-context requests (>30k tokens) from the same tenant during spike.

Alex M: looks like eviction -> regen -> latency feedback loop. Autoscaler didn't add nodes because cooldown + step limits prevented quick scale under this pattern. Policy "latency_target" has cooldown 120s and max_scale_step=1 for the pool.

SupportBot: Incident created: INC-2026-8571; assigned to eng-runtime.

Jamal R: repro steps I used locally: run 3 concurrent requests with 40k token contexts for tenant acme-retail. After ~90–120s you see eviction flood and 429s start. Command: ```./tools/repro --tenant acme-retail --concurrency 3 --ctx-len 40000 --duration 300 --pool gpu-pool-7```

Jamal R: quick reproduction logs show repeated cache miss -> regen -> write thrash on slab allocator, fragmentation increases ~0.4 -> 0.6 in minutes, then evictions spike.

Alex M: mitigation options: 1) temporarily isolate tenant to its own slab reserve, 2) bump reserved_cache_mb for tenant, or 3) trigger emergency burst (add a node) while we fix autoscaler. Which do we want to try now?

Ingrid S: I've applied a temporary config: set tenant_isolation=true and reserved_cache_mb=1024 for acme-retail on gpu-pool-7. Monitoring now.

Maria G: customer reports 429 rate dropped by ~80% after the change, but they still see occasional spikes on peak. They want a permanent fix.

Jamal R: engineering action items: 1) add fragmentation-aware compaction to the KV slab manager (prefer tenant-local compaction), 2) change eviction policy to be tenant-preferring LRU (avoid evicting many keys across multiple tenants during a single long-ctx stream), 3) update autoscaler to consider kv_eviction_rate and fragmentation as triggers (reduce cooldown to 30s and allow step=2 for emergency scaling). I'll open RFC+PRs.

Alex M: also recommend alerting: kvcache_eviction_rate > 100/s and fragmentation > 0.5 -> page oncall and emit high-priority incident. And billing: mark emergency burst as customer-protected so they aren't charged for the emergency node while we triage.

Maria G: noted. I'll update the support ticket with repro steps, the temp config we applied, and the customer's confirmation. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
